newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago boosted by recommendation, rumors.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago boosted by recommendation, rumors.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp stock has outperformed the stocks of many of its banking brethren in the last two weeks, boosted by a favorable analyst recommendation, improving credit card operations and a buyout rumor here and there.
From July 21 through Friday's close, First Chicago stock rose 16 percent compared to a seven percent gain in that time by the Standard & Poors bank index. The stock was up 5/16 at 75-7/8 Monday.

One factor that helped boost the stock was the decision by DLJ Securities to add the bank to its recommended list, saying among other things that "credit card profit growth should turn strongly positive due to lower loan losses."
"I think that had a lot to do with it," George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, said, linking the stock increase with the DLJ recommendation last week.
Also, bank stocks in general improved as interest rates went down, he noted.
But a rumor late last week that BankAmerica Corp might be in talks to acquire First Chicago also may have boosted the stock, analysts said, though they doubted the veracity of the rumor.
"I don't think there's anything behind it," Salem said, noting that anti-trust concerns in the Chicago market, where both banks operate, could scuttle any such deal.
Also, BankAmerica has adopted a strategy of being more focused on growing internal operations, despite its recent deal to acquire Robertson Stephens & Co, Salem noted.
"The odds are against it happening," said James Schutz, analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp.
Both First Chicago and BankAmerica declined comment on the rumor, citing company policy not to comment on market speculation.

While analysts were skeptical about the BankAmerica rumor, they noted that First Chicago could be an attractive target to another suitor, due to its strength in the Chicago, Detroit and Indianapolis markets.
"Anyone who has aspirations of having a national banking charter has to be interested in First Chicago," Schutz said.
That could mean NationsBank Corp could find First Chicago attractive, now that it has closed its acquisition of St. Louis-based Boatmen's Bancshares, analysts said.
"NationsBank just got finished with Boatmen's," Schutz said. "It's almost the logical step for them to make in the Midwest."
Analysts noted that there were rumors that NationsBank was eyeing First Chicago Corp two years ago before First Chicago and NBD Bancorp merged.

Whether First Chicago is willingly on the market less than two years after completing the merger is a key question. But in the rapidly consolidaitng financial industry, it is hard to rule out anything.
"They're all potential merger candidates at any point in time," Thomas Maier, analyst at EVEREN Securities, said.
